texts: bad: there is no supported form for a vague stretch of time, so 'many years' was silently downgraded to 'at least two years' — a far weaker claim than you wrote — and 'go back' can only reach a how-long-it-lasted slot, which is not how far back the records reach. State a figure and phrase it as a starting point: 'The Watch ledgers begin two hundred years before the present day.' (substitute the true figure; 'begin N years before the present day' has a proper carrier, 'go back many years' has none).

bad: the five listed items are packed into one recording event, which reads as a single joint act rather than five things the ledgers record, and the definite plural subject additionally forces a per-ledger rule that would claim every single ledger holds every category. Write one finite clause per item, with a singular subject for the collection: 'The ledger series records Council decisions. The ledger series records mire-essence reserve levels. The ledger series records feather store levels. The ledger series records apprentice entries. The ledger series records notable events.' Note the wording change from 'apprentice records' to 'apprentice entries': as written, that noun collapses onto the same symbol as the verb 'record' and will match recording-event questions spuriously.

bad: 'older' is a comparative with no stated standard (older than what?), which has no supported form and is dropped, so the parse says ledgers in general were stored there — wider than what you wrote. Use a plain adjective: 'The old ledgers were stored in the old Council hall.'
good. the hall is treated as one specific building with its age kept as a separate description, and the collapse lands as a past event with the hall as the thing that collapsed.

bad: same problem as the previous sentence — 'older' has no standard to compare against, so it is dropped and the parse claims the village lost ledgers in general rather than the old ones. Write 'The village lost old ledgers.'
